transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I keep getting pulled off track really easily. Like, I’ll be working on a dashboard, and then a Slack notification or even a song lyric or some random project idea pops up, and I just lose the thread of what I was doing.
Did you have the same kind of trouble staying focused when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. In elementary school, teachers would write things like that I rushed through worksheets or didn’t follow all the directions. And during group stuff I’d talk over people sometimes.

My parents also had to sit with me during homework, because if they didn’t, I’d kind of drift off or start doing something else before I finished.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?
Um… I don’t think so. I’ve had nights where I stayed up too late, but not like I felt unusually energized or didn’t need sleep.
Do these focus problems interfere with your work or daily responsibilities?

Yeah… it does. I’m not working a regular job right now, but with freelance stuff, I’ve lost a couple small contracts because I didn’t follow through cleanly. And I missed out on a portfolio competition, too.

It’s… frustrating, because people like my ideas, but some friends or collaborators are kind of hesitant to work with me now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed a lot lately?
Not really… I mean, I get frustrated with myself, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed a lot.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying?
Not really a lot, no. I mean, I worry about stuff when I’m behind or I messed something up, but I don’t think it’s constant.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern of distractibility and difficulty sustaining attention that began in childhood and currently causes academic/occupational impairment. Childhood history includes rushing through work, not following directions, drifting off during homework, and talking over others, supporting ADHD with predominant inattentive symptoms and some hyperactive/impulsive features. Mood and anxiety symptoms were not prominent, and there was no evidence of manic episodes to suggest an alternative explanation.
